paper_metadata.title: Microstructure, tribological property and high temperature tensile property of Co-Cr-Ni-W alloy parts fabricated by laser directed energy deposition

evidence.quote: Co-Cr-Ni-W alloy parts were fabricated on the surface of 304 stainless steel (SS) substrate by laser directed energy deposition (LDED).
Chemical composition of W6Mo5Cr4V2Co5 cobalt-containing high-speed steel.
The powder for LDED was commercial Co-Cr-Ni-W alloy powder with the particle size of 80 – 200 μ m.
The samples were placed in Muffle furnace at 750 ◦C, 850 ◦C and 950 ◦C for 5 h respectively, then cooled in air.

When martensitic and carbide precipitation form in the alloy, microhardness and wear resistance would be improved by the second phase strengthening.

According to the Orowan mechanism, when there are nanoscale second phase particles in the matrix, they will hinder the movement of dislocations when the metal is impacted, improving the matrix's ability to resist external shock, and thereby increasing the hardness of the metal.

When martensitic and carbide precipitation form in the alloy, microhardness and wear resistance would be improved by the second phase strengthening.

According to the Orowan mechanism, when there are nanoscale second phase particles in the matrix, they will hinder the movement of dislocations when the metal is impacted, improving the matrix's ability to resist external shock, and thereby increasing the hardness of the metal.

It is noticed that under the same temperature, the ultimate tensile stress and yield stress of Co-Cr-Ni-W alloy are significantly higher than those of high-speed steel, and tensile property of two materials are both decrease with the temperature increasing.
